DECISION 
 
2. 
The appeal was dismissed. 
 
3. 
The panel found that Flat 3, 2 Westbeech Road should remain in the council tax valuation 
list. 
 
STATEMENT OF REASONS 
 
Introduction 
 
4. 
This appeal had been brought in respect of the following: the appellant was the owner and 
council taxpayer of the appeal property Flat 3, 2 Westbeech Road, London N22 6HT and had 
been since 25 June 2012. The property was in band A with effect from 25 June 2012. 
 
5. 
The appellant had submitted a proposal on 14 April 2025 to delete the property from 16 
January 2025 from the council tax valuation list because it could not lawfully be occupied as 
it was too small.  
 
6. 
The listing officer (LO) issued her decision notice on 8 October 2025 to maintain the property 
in the list. 
 
7. 
The appellant appealed to the tribunal on 9 January 2026.  
 
8. 
To assist the appellant and with the agreement of the parties, the tribunal panel varied its 
model procedure and invited the LO’s representative to present his case first. 
 
9. 
This tribunal decision document is not and does not purport to be a verbatim record of 
proceedings. 
 
Issue 
10. The issue for the panel to determine was whether Flat 3, 2 Westbeech Road, London N22 
6HT should be deleted from toe council tax list.  
 
Relevant Law 
 
11. Local Government Finance Act 1992. 
 
12. The Council Tax (Situation and Valuation of Dwellings) Regulations 1992 [S.I. 1992 No. 550] 
as amended.  
 
13. Wilson v Coll (LO) [2011] EWHC 2824 (Admin). 
 
Discussion 
 
14. The respondent had provided a consolidated evidence bundle totalling containing the 
information which had been exchanged between the parties prior to the hearing. This 
included a copy of the proposal, the appeal, the decision notice, photographs of the appeal 
property and extracts from the relevant legislation and case law. The date on which to 
consider the appeal property, the proposed effective date, was 16 January 2025.  
 

[2026] VTE VT00033508 (CVAD)

3/4 
www.valuationtribunal.gov.uk 
15. The appellant’s representative had stated that the property was last used on 15 January 
2025 and the WC facilities were removed on 16 January 2025. The billing authority (BA), 
Haringey Council, had undertaken a review of lettable properties in its area and found that 
the appeal property was too small to be rented out as a flat. The BA required a minimum of 
13m2 in area and the flat was only 9m2. The licence to let the flat was revoked on 20 June 
2025 and the room was now used as a utility room. 
 
16. For these reasons the appellant wanted the property deleted from the council tax list. 
 
17. The respondent’s representative had stated that the appeal property remained intact, was 
wind and watertight, was not derelict, there was no scheme of works being undertaken and it 
was in reasonable repair. There was no reason to delete the appeal property as it remained 
to be a dwelling for the purposes of council tax.  
 
18. The panel noted that the appeal property had been in the council tax valuation list since 25 
June 2012 as a council tax dwelling and had been let out until January 2025. The panel was 
aware that the size of the dwelling was not a part of its consideration, that had only been 
relevant to the BA’s own procedures, it had no bearing on the appeal property as a council 
tax dwelling.  
 
19. In considering whether a hereditament exists the panel referred to the case of Wilson v Coll 
that asked the question of whether, having regard to the character of the property and a 
reasonable amount of repair, the premises could be occupied as a dwelling. The panel found 
that this was only related to whether the appeal property was a dwelling or not and issues of 
minimum space standards, licensing restrictions, or the legal permissibility of occupation 
under housing legislation was not relevant. 
 
20. The panel found that the appeal property had been a hereditament and therefore a dwelling 
for council tax purposes since 25 January 2012 and remained to be a hereditament and a 
dwelling for council tax purposes on 16 January 2025.  
 
Decision  
 
21. The panel found that the appeal property must remain in the council tax valuation list and the 
appeal was therefore dismissed. 
 
Right of further appeal 
 
22. Any party who is aggrieved at the Tribunal’s decision has a statutory right of further appeal to 
the High Court on a point of law pursuant to Regulation 43 of the Tribunal Procedure 
Regulations. A party does not require permission to appeal from the Tribunal. Any appeal 
must be made directly to the High Court using Form N161 (Appellant’s Notice) within four 
weeks of the date this decision and statement of reasons was issued. 
 
23. Further information regarding this statutory right of further appeal, and the parties’ other 
rights, is contained in the guidance booklet “A guide to tribunal decisions” available on the 
Tribunal’s website at www.valuationtribunal.gov.uk/guidance-booklets/.
